focus: Explain binary-response logistic probability from a linear score z = intercept + weight times input and p = 1/(1+exp(-z)). Let learners change the score components and compare z, odds exp(z), and the resulting probability, emphasizing that the probability remains between zero and one.
audience: A second-year engineering undergraduate familiar with linear functions, exponentials, and probability.
excerpt: Paraphrase, not a quotation: the case illustrates a modern logistic sigmoid mapping a real-valued score to probability. Cox's abstract supports modeling binary outcomes as a function of explanatory variables; the full article and this exact displayed equation were not verified in the accessible abstract.
section: Cox (1958), The Regression Analysis of Binary Sequences, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 20(2), pp. 215–232, summary/abstract. Publisher page and abstract accessible; full text may require subscription.
